title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
statement: Given an integer list nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence — a sequence of elements picked from nums in order (not necessarily contiguous) where each element is strictly greater than the previous one. An empty list has an answer of 0.
hints: The naive 1-D dp where dp[i] is the longest increasing subsequence ending at i takes O(n^2); there is a faster O(n log n) approach worth reaching for.

Maintain an array 'tails' where tails[k] is the smallest possible tail value of any increasing subsequence of length k+1 seen so far; tails stays sorted, so each new number can be placed with binary search.

For each x in nums, binary-search for the leftmost position in tails that is >= x; if x extends past the end, append it (a new longest length), otherwise overwrite that position; the final length of tails is the answer.
